dashboard.title: Ultrafast charge transfer in layered matter
dashboard.focusTitle: The caption and results differ by 12 fs
dashboard.summary: The Figure 3C fit records 68 fs while the results currently state 80 fs. Both remain linked to the raw frames and calibration record; choose the supported wording before recording the next version.
dashboard.eventOneNote: Parameter bounds and calibration records linked.
dashboard.eventTwoNote: The caption and result use different time constants.
dashboard.eventThreeNote: Four files entered the evidence library.

editor.paragraphOne: We measured interlayer charge transfer with few-cycle pump-probe microscopy, constraining time zero through three independent calibrations. Every run retains raw frames, calibration parameters and the analysis environment.
editor.paragraphTwo: Fitting is limited to regions above the preregistered signal-to-noise threshold. The method resolves a fast channel before structural relaxation, but cannot determine its microscopic mechanism alone.
editor.note: Keeping reproducibility conditions beside the prose makes them easier to find than hiding them in a low-contrast settings panel.

review.quote: All three independent calibration runs resolve an early transfer component below 80 fs.
review.title: Keep the conclusion inside the evidence boundary
review.body: The current sentence presents the fast component as a confirmed mechanism, while the evidence supports only its time scale and repeatability. Keep the observation and leave mechanism for later validation.
review.before: We confirm a phonon-driven ultrafast interlayer transfer mechanism.
review.after: We observe an interlayer transfer component below 80 fs across three independent calibrations.

explore.oneTitle: Nonequilibrium carrier dynamics in layered semiconductors
explore.twoTitle: How time-zero calibration changes sub-100-fs claims
explore.threeNote: Preprint · four public reviews · CC0 data · 2026

reading.title: Ultrafast charge transfer in layered matter
reading.deck: An evidence-first versioned record connecting claims, methods, raw data and reproducible environments.
reading.paragraphOne: How interlayer charge moves before the lattice reaches equilibrium is central to nonequilibrium processes in two-dimensional heterostructures. Each primary claim stays in the same version as the raw frames, calibration record and analysis code that produced it.
reading.paragraphTwo: Three independent runs show a transfer component below 80 femtoseconds. The result supports an early channel but does not determine the microscopic mechanism alone; that limitation remains visible beside the reproduction conditions.
